5.10.validation: 2026.11.6.20 makes the install mode decide every layout question. A normal install (force_layout=0) always uses the layout compiled for its branch and never reads BTF, because a normal package matches its build tree. A force-adapted install (force_layout=1) resolves thread.debug from BTF and falls back to a read-only disassembly probe of flush_ptrace_hw_breakpoint. On 6.1 the same forced path also resolves the four input_dev members that move when a vendor grows struct work_struct (h_list/node/num_vals/timestamp): BTF first, otherwise the sizeof(struct input_dev) immediate in input_allocate_device; other fields are checked against the compiled offsets and a mismatch disables touch instead of misreading. The 6.1_vivo package is gone and one 6.1 package serves both GKI and vivo. Verified on V2352A 6.1.145: forced logs debug 0x1370 and input h_list=0x5d8 node=0x5e8 num_vals=0x5f8 timestamp=0x610 size=1616, and CTF_OPEN succeeds; normal logs compiled 0x1120 / 0x5d0 0x5e0 0x5f0 0x608. The 5.10 branch also writes /sys/rsc/qos/qos_enable and qos_cpu_enable to 0 at load and never restores them, avoiding the vivo RSC SVP scheduler brk #0x5512 on CE wake (V2232A verified).

6.18.validation: 6.18.21 android17 common tree f957accaf563 compiled with gki_defconfig (4K pages, PREEMPT, MODVERSIONS, BTI/PAC, no LTO); 6.18 removed register_user_step_hook, so the EL0 single-step callback is taken over by rewriting the single BL arm64_force_sig_fault inside do_el0_softstep (located by the adjacent mov w0,#5 / mov w1,#2) into a core B to a newly allocated immutable gateway page in the +/-128 MiB vmalloc window; the gateway jumps absolutely into the module stub, which saves the full register file, dispatches in C and rewrites its resume tail into an absolute jump back to gateway+64 -> BL+4. Perf event re-enable is deferred to TWA_RESUME because perf_event_enable sleeps. If any step of the install fails the whole PTE/CE single-step feature is refused (fail-closed) instead of advertising support. Also: maps path buffer 256->512 with only the trailing " (deleted)" suffix trimmed, arch_vma_name fallback when vm_ops->name is NULL, and BSS lookup now trims that suffix too. vermagic rewritten to the device release; __versions cleared; no static percpu; 2026.11.4.2 removes task_work_add from the import table (vendor kernels list it as a protected symbol and reject the load with -EACCES "Unresolved symbol task_work_add"); it is now resolved through kallsyms like the other private helpers; rebuilt with -fsanitize-cfi-icall-experimental-normalize-integers so KCFI type hashes match Android 17 6.18 GKI CONFIG_CFI_ICALL_NORMALIZE_INTEGERS=y (the previous package was built without it and mismatched integer-typed callbacks), vermagic rewritten to the target device release, struct module layout checked against the device BTF (size 1664, init 376, exit 1536), and handshake/version/read/write/maps/module-base verified on REDMAGIC NX819J 6.18.21-android17-5-gedb80646c73d; 2026.11.6.1 unifies this 6.18 baseline with the shared 5.10-6.12 source: every user single step is tracked in a 16-slot ownership ledger (including the gateway no-bp path) and the thread_struct.debug offsets are resolved from /sys/kernel/btf/vmlinux at init instead of compiled offsets; the import set is unchanged from 2026.11.5.1; 2026.11.6.2 calls kernel_read through a __nocfi wrapper so a vendor kernel with a different kCFI type hash for kernel_read cannot panic at init (enforced-CFI 5.15 reproduced); all other kallsyms-resolved helpers already used __nocfi wrappers; 2026.11.6.3 applies the stability audit: __nocfi sme helper, raw-spinlock step ledger with reserve-before-enable and TIF-aware sweep, gateway restore verified before vfree, type-id based BTF layout validation with bitfield rejection, workqueue-deferred CE session free, and init-failure unwind; 2026.11.6.4 removes the unused HEZI/GUO legacy ioctls (40-44) and their handlers, and hwliming.h drops the matching API; 2026.11.6.5 applies the re-audit: per-section BTF length limits (the old str_off+str_len check rejected real ARM64 BTF), u16 magic + exact version/flags, and the legacy active_bp/deferred perf branch removed from the gateway dispatcher; 2026.11.6.6 carries the shared re-audit fixes (pid-handle registry, RCU SIGUSR1 scan, age-based step ledger that rejects stale claims, fail-closed step reservation, stricter BTF member decoding); 2026.11.6.7 completes N01: the gateway core BL is published only as the last init step, a module reference is held for as long as the entry exists, an unconfirmed core read-back keeps the gateway and module body and never advertises the feature, LM_DRIVER_RESTORE detaches with read-back confirmation before the module becomes visible (a failed detach leaves delete_module blocked), and LM_DRIVER_HIDE re-arms the entry after visibility-only restores; 2026.11.6.8 rebuilds 6.18 from the final synchronized tree (capability withdrawn before the core word is touched, module reference dropped last); 5.10-6.12 differ from 6.7 only by the version string; 2026.11.6.9 applies the 6.8 static review: CE session reclaim is always deferred (no voluntary schedule inside the gateway trampoline), RESTORE/HIDE are visibility-only, LM_DRIVER_PREPARE_UNLOAD detaches only with no CE/PTE session or core patch left, the dock thread is created parked and woken after init commits, the native step hook is unregistered only if registered, and the time-based per-task step ledger is removed; 2026.11.6.10 uses a dedicated CE reclaim workqueue drained before module text can go away, closes CE/PTE admission in the PREPARE_UNLOAD transaction, records the origin of the native-call recovery step so it is not delivered as SIGTRAP, and rejects CE attach/step on a tracer-owned thread; 2026.11.6.11 makes the client poll the result word at offset 12 (the old loop already waited for the driver 0x5201314 ack) and the SIGUSR1 scan no longer reads/prints per-process cmdlines, skips kernel threads, looks up maps once and compares VMA dentry names instead of d_path; si_pid is unusable because the kernel skips siginfo for PF_KTHREAD targets; 2026.11.6.12 sizes the SIGUSR1 task snapshot from an RCU count instead of the fixed 1024 entries, so a late-created dock process is still scanned on devices with more than 1024 tasks (the actual dock-timeout root cause)
